heroHeadline: Trump Orders, Then Cancels, US Strikes on Houthis After Saudi Plea — Mecca Pact Allies Offer Words, Not Forces
heroSubtitle: President Trump ordered the Pentagon to prepare airstrikes on Houthi targets following a phone call with Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, with target lists approved and munitions loaded onto aircraft, before reversing course at the last minute and calling off the strikes. Trump said Washington maintains direct channels with the Houthis and that the group had agreed not to engage US forces; Houthi political bureau member Mohamed al-Bukhaiti confirmed indirect, Oman-mediated contact, saying the group is "not targeting the United States, or any other nation, in the strait, with the sole exception of the Saudi enemy." The episode reinforces a pattern six weeks into the Mecca pact: Saudi Arabia's default crisis channel remains bilateral appeals to Washington rather than activation of the trilateral pact's own machinery, with Pakistan and Turkey left out of the strike deliberations entirely and still offering only rhetorical or technical-assistance support.
